    Required labeled sample size for PPI++ (mean estimator or OLS contrast)

    n_required_ppi_pp.Rd

    Computes the minimum number of labeled observations \(n\) required to achieve a desired power for Prediction-Powered Plus (PPI++) inference.

    The function supports:

    • Mean estimation (scalar parameter)

    • OLS linear contrast estimation \(a^\top \beta\)

    and three modes for the augmentation weight \(\lambda\):

    • "vanilla" — \(\lambda = 1\) (standard PPI)

    • "oracle" — \(\lambda = \lambda^\star\) (variance-minimizing; ratio \(r = n/N\) updated iteratively)

    • "user" — \(\lambda = \lambda_{\text{user}}\) (user-specified)

    The unlabeled sample size \(N\) contributes predictions \(f(X)\) that reduce the variance of the estimator. The function uses closed-form inversions when available, or numerical root-finding otherwise, to compute the minimal \(n\) satisfying the desired power constraint.

    n_required_ppi_pp(
  delta,
  N,
  alpha = 0.05,
  power = 0.8,
  type = c("mean", "ols"),
  lambda_mode = c("vanilla", "oracle", "user"),
  lambda_user = NULL,
  sigma_y2 = NULL,
  sigma_f2 = NULL,
  cov_y_f = NULL,
  var_f = NULL,
  var_res = NULL,
  metrics = NULL,
  metric_type = NULL,
  m_labeled = NULL,
  correction = TRUE,
  c = NULL,
  H_L = NULL,
  H_U = NULL,
  Sigma_YY = NULL,
  Sigma_ff_l = NULL,
  Sigma_ff_u = NULL,
  Sigma_Yf = NULL,
  warn_smallN = TRUE,
  smallN_threshold = 500,
  mode = c("error", "cap")
)

    Arguments

    delta

    Numeric scalar. Effect size being tested.

    • Mean case: \(\theta - \theta_0\).

    • OLS case: \(a^\top \beta - \theta_0\). Must be nonzero.

    N

    Positive scalar. Size of the unlabeled dataset used to compute \(\bar f_U\). Must satisfy N > 0.

    alpha

    Significance level for a two-sided Wald test. Default: 0.05.

    power

    Desired statistical power, e.g., 0.80.

    type

    Character string specifying the estimation problem:

    • "mean" — mean estimator \(\hat{\theta}_\lambda\).

    • "ols" — linear contrast \(a^\top \hat{\beta}_\lambda\).

    lambda_mode

    Character string specifying λ:

    • "vanilla" — λ = 1.

    • "oracle" — λ = λ\*(n), updated using r = n/N.

    • "user" — λ fixed at user-supplied lambda_user.

    lambda_user

    Numeric. The λ value to use when lambda_mode = "user". Otherwise ignored.

    sigma_y2

    Variance of the labeled outcomes \(Y\). Optional if using metrics.

    sigma_f2

    Variance of the predictions \(f(X)\). Optional if using metrics.

    cov_y_f

    Covariance between \(Y\) and \(f(X)\).

    var_f

    Alias for sigma_f2. Provided for flexibility.

    var_res

    Residual variance \(\Var(Y - f(X))\). Used if available.

    metrics

    Optional list containing predictive performance summaries such as:

    • mean squared error (MSE)

    • \(R^2\)

    • empirical covariance estimates Used as an alternative interface when sigma_* are not provided.

    metric_type

    Character. One of "continuous" or "binary". Determines how prediction metrics are translated to required moments.

    m_labeled

    Number of labeled samples used to estimate prediction metrics. Needed for small-sample corrections.

    correction

    Logical. If TRUE (default), applies finite-sample corrections to adjust \(\sigma_f^2\) and \(\Cov(Y,f)\).

    c

    Numeric vector defining the contrast \(a\). Must have length p.

    H_L

    Per-observation Hessians for labeled design matrices.

    H_U

    Per-observation Hessians for labeled and unlabeled design matrices. For OLS, \(H = X^\top X / n\). These are used in the sandwich variance formula.

    Sigma_YY

    Sandwich covariance term \(\Sigma_{YY}\).

    Sigma_ff_l

    Sandwich covariance terms \(\Sigma_{ff}\) computed on labeled samples.

    Sigma_ff_u

    Sandwich covariance terms \(\Sigma_{ff}\) computed on unlabeled samples.

    Sigma_Yf

    Cross-covariance sandwich term \(\Sigma_{Yf}\).

    warn_smallN

    Logical. If TRUE, warns when N < smallN_threshold.

    smallN_threshold

    Numeric threshold at which to trigger a warning (default: 500).

    mode

    How to behave if the required n exceeds N:

    • "error" — throw an error (default)

    • "cap" — return n = N and attach attribute "achieved_power".

    Value

    Integer labeled sample size n_star. When mode = "cap" and n_star > N, returns N and attaches attr(n_star, "achieved_power").

    Examples

    
metrics <- list(
  type = "continuous",
  mse = 0.6,
  var_y = 1.0,
  cov_y_f = 0.18,
  m_obs = 300
)

n_required_ppi_pp(
  delta = 0.25, N = 5000,
  type = "mean",
  metrics = metrics,
  metric_type = "continuous",
  lambda_mode = "vanilla"
)
#> [1] 132

n_required_ppi_pp(
  delta = 0.25, N = 5000,
  type = "mean",
  sigma_y2 = 1.0,
  sigma_f2 = 0.4,
  cov_y_f  = 0.18,
  var_f    = 0.4,          # must supply
  var_res  = 1.0 - 0.4,    # = 0.6
  lambda_mode = "oracle"
)
#> [1] 116

n_required_ppi_pp(
  delta = 0.25, N = 5000,
  type = "mean",
  sigma_y2 = 1.0,
  sigma_f2 = 0.4,
  cov_y_f  = 0.18,
  var_f = 0.4,
  var_res = 0.6,
  lambda_mode = "user",
  lambda_user = 0.5
)
#> [1] 116

p <- 3
cvec <- c(1, 0, -1)
Hpop <- diag(p)
SYY  <- diag(p)
Sff  <- 0.5 * diag(p)
SYf  <- 0.3 * diag(p)
 
## Vanilla λ=1
n_required_ppi_pp(
  delta = 0.15, N = 2000,
  type = "ols",
  c = cvec,
  H_L = Hpop, H_U = Hpop,
  Sigma_YY = SYY,
  Sigma_ff_l = Sff, Sigma_ff_u = Sff,
  Sigma_Yf   = SYf,
  lambda_mode = "vanilla"
)
#> [1] 761

## Oracle λ*
n_required_ppi_pp(
  delta = 0.15, N = 2000,
  type = "ols",
  c = cvec,
  H_L = Hpop, H_U = Hpop,
  Sigma_YY = SYY,
  Sigma_ff_l = Sff, Sigma_ff_u = Sff,
  Sigma_Yf   = SYf,
  lambda_mode = "oracle"
)
#> [1] 602
